Hi [Name] - I run Parallax Data Lab in Cincinnati. I help teams fix the layer underneath dashboards: KPI definitions, reporting logic, ownership, and the operating cadence that turns numbers into decisions. I noticed [company-specific context]. If reporting trust, metric debates, or manual recurring reporting is creating drag, would a 15-minute fit check be worth it next week?

Hi, this is Jonah with Parallax Data Lab. I help operations and finance teams clean up reporting friction when dashboards exist but leaders still debate the numbers. Who owns KPI reporting or analytics operations for your team?

I help Cincinnati/regional teams turn dashboard sprawl and metric debates into trusted operating scorecards. Reaching out because your team looks like the kind where reporting clarity can move decisions faster.

Do not walk into hospitals, banks, enterprise campuses, or regulated facilities. For local family-owned or mid-market public-office targets, bring a one-page Dashboard Trust Scorecard and say you are leaving it for the person who owns reporting/operations.
Ask for a 15-minute Fit Check, not a paid project. Keep the ask small.
Send the Dashboard Trust Scorecard or a short article like 'Why Nobody Trusts Your Dashboard' when the company appears to have dashboard trust pain.
Do not open with 'I build dashboards.' That positions you as a commodity Power BI freelancer. Open with trust, decisions, metric ownership, and operating clarity.
8:15-9:15 AM for operations leaders; 11:00-11:45 AM for finance/analytics follow-up; 3:30-4:45 PM for second call block.
Worth a quick look, or is dashboard/reporting ownership handled cleanly already? If it is not a priority, I can close the loop.

Sharing this scorecard because it is a simple way to identify whether the issue is metric trust, ownership, source reliability, decision cadence, or operational signal. Happy to compare notes if useful.
